heading: Pick a model by what you care about
mobileHint: Tap or drag the triangle to set your priorities.
mapDescription: A triangle of hexagons. Each corner puts all 12 units on Smart, Time or Cost. Each color shows the top model for that mix among the checked creators. Use the arrow keys to move between hexagons and Enter to pick one. Each preset is a pin: tab to it, move it with the arrow keys, and press Enter to use it.
presetHint: Drag a pin on the triangle to move a preset.
creatorsHint: Only models from checked creators can win a hexagon or appear in the table. Regret is still measured against the Full Catalog frontier, so unchecking a creator removes rivals without rescoring anyone. The search box below only filters the table.
caption: {count} frontier models · top: {top}
captionEmpty: No frontier models · no creators checked
emptyCreators: No creators are checked, so there is no model to rank. Open Creators above and check at least one, or choose Select all.
whyIntro: Each number is a weighted regret: the model's gap from the best Full Catalog frontier value on that axis, divided by that frontier's interquartile range, times the axis's share of power. Regret has no units, and lower is better.
whyScore: Worst regret {value}. The largest weighted regret is the limiting trade-off: it sets the rank, and ties go to the lower mean weighted regret.
whyScoreTied: Worst regret {value}, shared by {axes}. Together they are the limiting trade-off: they set the rank, and ties go to the lower mean weighted regret.
whyNoRegret: Worst regret {value}. This model has the best Full Catalog frontier value on every axis with power, so no trade-off limits it.
whyDominated: {name} ({creator}) dominates this model among the checked creators. Compared with this model, {name} is:
hexNoModel: no model, because no creators are checked
explainRanking: The page ranks models in two steps. First it keeps only models from the creators checked under Creators, then drops every one that another checked model matches or beats on every axis you gave power to and beats on at least one of them. The models left over form the Pareto frontier. An axis with zero power plays no part in this step or the next.
Then it sorts the frontier by interquartile minimax regret, using your allocation as the weights. The model whose worst case is least bad comes first.

Each hexagon is one way to split the 12 units in whole steps, and its color is the model that ranks first there. Click or tap a hexagon to use its split. Drag across the triangle to move in quarter units. The table above lists the frontier for the current split. The search box only narrows the table: it never changes the triangle or the ranking. The ring marks the current split, which can sit between hexagons.
explainRegret: For each axis, a model's regret is how far it sits from the best value on the Full Catalog frontier: the frontier of every model in the catalog, whichever creators are checked. That gap is divided by the interquartile range of the axis across that frontier, so a gap counts as big or small relative to how spread out the frontier is. Time uses a log scale, so halving the time counts the same whether a task takes ten seconds or ten minutes. Because this yardstick never changes with your creator choice, unchecking a creator removes rivals but leaves every other model's regret the same.

Each axis's regret is then multiplied by that axis's share of the 12 units. A model's score is its largest weighted regret, and ties go to the lower mean weighted regret. The lowest score wins. Regret has no units, and lower is better. Open Why this model? on any row to see its weighted regret on each axis.
Put simply, the top model is the one that is never far behind on anything you care about.
explainMetricsTitle: How Smart, Time and Cost are measured
explainMetricsIntro: Every number comes straight from the catalog, with no adjustment by this page.
explainData: This page uses {name}, version {version}, generated on {date}.
explainEmbedded: The page carries a stripped copy of the catalog: each model's name, creator, release date and three metrics. It makes no network requests, so it works offline and sends nothing anywhere. Rebuild the page to pick up new data.
footerMethod: Pareto frontier over the axes with power, then interquartile minimax regret.
